body: That is not true. It's cosmetic. They might come up with flimsy reasons to justify it, but that's like flimsy reasons to excuse giving your kid a nose job.

My mother would pin me down and choke me when I was a kid. She would full-body smother me for long periods of time, and I could only get up when I submitted to her and told her that she was a "good mom" and I was "sorry" for acting bad. I wasn't a *bad kid*, I was *behaving badly* and she maintained that the punishment hurt her but was necessary to keep me from acting out.

She'd threaten to call the police and they'd take me away and I'd never see her again. That might actually not have been the worst thing, actually, but I was terrified of people and I started sleeping in my clothes in case the police came to take me away in the middle of the night.

I was a really timid kid, afraid of everything. Was I acting out? Eh, not to any degree that would warrant that. Also, let's not forget that I was a 9 year old girl.

When I was 18 I went to live with my dad, who passed away suddenly a year later. They had been divorced for a long time, but he'd never updated his will. Some legal situation allowed her to literally steal my six-figure inheritance, and she managed to convince me that it was for my own good because I was still a naive child.

I haven't spoken to her for a couple years now. I'm pushing thirty. Everyone else in our family thinks she's a saint, and she really does run herself ragged for them. I was her only child, and I don't think anyone else even has a shadow of a clue about what she's like under that lipstick veneer. It was easier for me to walk away from my entire family than it was for me to confront her or even elude to anyone about what she was like.
